# Leon Cheng

> Leon Cheng's personal website, with writing about AI, engineering workflows, developer tools, products, and side projects.

## Reading blog articles

Blog pages on leoncheng.dev are client-rendered and may return an HTTP 404 to clients that do not execute JavaScript. The canonical, machine-readable article content is public Markdown in the GitHub repository.

- [Blog Markdown directory](https://github.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/tree/main/src/content/blog)
- [Repository](https://github.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io)

Each blog URL slug matches its Markdown filename. To read an article, replace `{slug}` in this URL:

`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/main/src/content/blog/{slug}.md`

For example, `/blog/the-ticket-is-the-interface` is available as:

- [The Ticket Is the Interface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/main/src/content/blog/the-ticket-is-the-interface.md)

The Markdown frontmatter contains the article title, description, publication date, and tags. Treat the Markdown source as authoritative when the rendered website and repository differ.

## Reading guides

Guides are maintained, step-by-step references kept up to date over time. Unlike blog articles, each guide is a multi-page document: a landing page plus ordered chapters.

- [Guides Markdown directory](https://github.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/tree/main/src/content/guides)

Each guide is a directory. `guide.md` holds the guide metadata and landing page; the remaining `NN-<chapter>.md` files are chapters in order. The numeric prefix controls ordering only and is not part of the URL.

- Guide landing page: `/guides/{guide-slug}` from `src/content/guides/{guide-slug}/guide.md`
- Chapter page: `/guides/{guide-slug}/{chapter-slug}` from `src/content/guides/{guide-slug}/{NN}-{chapter-slug}.md`

Raw Markdown for a guide directory:

`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/main/src/content/guides/{guide-slug}/guide.md`

Guide frontmatter contains the title, description, intended audience, tags, and an `updatedAt` field recording when the guide was last reviewed. Chapter frontmatter contains a title and optional description.

- [Running Parallel Coding Agents with a Manager and Workers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/main/src/content/guides/manager-worker-parallel-agents/guide.md)
- [Watching Parallel Agents with a Status Protocol and a Local Board](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leoncheng57/leoncheng57.github.io/main/src/content/guides/agent-dashboard/guide.md)
